frequency_question: How often do minority-sponsored restrictive voting bills pass the U.S. Senate within a one-year window?
membership_rule: Federal bills sponsored primarily by the minority party in the Senate aimed at altering voter eligibility requirements, evaluated over a rolling 1-year window from introduction.

cases.name: National Voter Registration Act restrictive amendments (historical baseline)

provenance_note: claims 30 cases from only 3 named (10.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 3 named legislative vehicles; estimated ~30 comparable partisan legislative pushes over 30 years.
known_gaps: Exact tracking of every single minor rider or amendment is difficult, but major standalone bills are fully accounted for.
skeleton: Minority-sponsored highly partisan electoral bills introduced in divided or opposition-controlled Senates over the last 30 years.
multiplier: Estimated ~10 major comparable partisan attempts per decade, yielding approximately 30 total instances, with 0 successful passages due to filibuster and party polarization.
validity_reason: Filibuster rules and intense partisan polarization in the Senate remain stable structural features for the medium term.
